business_problem: Foxconn needed to reduce nurse burnout and repetitive transport work in hospitals, but deploying autonomous clinical robots required safe simulation, real-time edge perception, and dependable navigation inside busy wards.
solution_summary: Foxconn built Nurabot with the NVIDIA Isaac for Healthcare framework so hospitals could shift repetitive transport and logistics work away from nurses. The solution starts in digital twin hospital environments created with Isaac Sim and Omniverse, where Foxconn tests workflows, navigation, and model behavior before field deployment. Once validated, Nurabot runs in wards on Jetson AGX Orin edge compute, using multimodal perception, natural-language interaction, and real-time sensor processing to move medication, specimens, and supplies autonomously. The broader stack also uses Holoscan for real-time data handling and Cosmos-based scheduling and route optimization, while DGX infrastructure supports training for tasks such as audio classification and action recognition. That architecture let Foxconn move from simulation-driven validation into live pilots at Taichung Veterans General Hospital and then extend the model toward broader smart-hospital rollouts.

The resulting models are deployed onto Jetson AGX Orin-powered robots that process ward sensor data locally, navigate autonomously, and return operational feedback that informs wider hospital rollouts.
